text: This service reads collateral, appraisal, balance and score facts only through the rwb-source-data contract, publishes nothing it read from a view, and keeps the FSD field names (v_ace_valuation.*, v_ace_collateral.*, v_ace_score.*) as the source field names that contract returns.
why: Arch v5 (higher in precedence) makes the 30 views readable by rwb-source-data alone and gives the S1 row one REST call, to P1.
read: FSD S1 integration points and field catalog as a statement of which facts the decision needs, not of how they are read.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 3; Section 6 FR-S1-001 to FR-S1-004, FR-S1-014, FR-S1-027; Section 8.2; Section 9
confirm: Solution architect with P1, before wave 3 system test
impact: If a view stays readable by this service, the boundary test and the freshness guarantee would both need a second owner.

text: The appraisal acceptance is held in this service's own valuation record and the P1 extension row is read and written through the source-data contract; this service never writes schema rwb_source_data, and P1's OQ-P1-05 stays open.
why: The Ownership Map gives valuation_ext to P1 and keeps the writer of the stale flag and the age open.
read: FSD S1 A2.4 to A2.11 as an acceptance requirement, with the storage read as P1's extension table behind a contract.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S1-004; Section 6 FR-S1-010; Section 8.1; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S1-02
confirm: Data architect with P1, before wave 3 system test
impact: Two writers of one acceptance row would make the value band and the stale flag disagree.

text: This service owns the three entity groups that Architecture v5 names (valuations, the D6 route decision and the route agent output) in schema rwb_valuation, and no physical table name is stated because the Ownership Map lists none.
why: Arch v5 slides 18 and 41 give the schema and the three things it holds; the map has no S1 table row.
read: Arch v5 slide 18's list of what the schema holds as the entity set, with the physical names left to the DB story.
confirm: Data architect, before the S1 DB story
impact: The migration and the boundary test cannot be written until the table set exists; the story that creates it is not blocked.

text: RouteDecided is published on rwb.valuation.events.v1, keyed by caseId, as a CloudEvent through the outbox, without an EV number until the event catalogue allocates one.
why: Arch v5 slides 18 and 43 name the event and the topic; the map has no row for it.
read: Arch v5 slide 43's additional event row as a producer contract, with the register entry to follow.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S1-012; Section 6 FR-S1-025; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S1-04
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 system test
impact: Without the event a case cannot move on an approved route, so the consumer test is blocked, not the build.

text: The valuation read is carried as GET /cases/{id}/valuation and the command as POST /cases/{id}/route-proposals per Architecture v5 slide 18, with POST /cases/{caseId}/route read as the same command; one path is fixed in the contract story.
why: The slide, the API specification and the map disagree on the names, and the slide is highest in precedence.
read: FSD S1 A2.7 to A2.9 as one recommendation step and one approval step behind two operations.
confirm: Solution architect, before the S1 CON story is closed
impact: A path change after the screen is built costs a gateway route and a client change.

text: The two asset valuation operations belong to this service, and rwb-asset reads the accepted appraisal through this service's contract for the floor price and the monthly re-appraisal.
why: The Ownership Map ruling moves the paths to S1 because Arch v5 gives rwb-valuation the valuations (ASM-A6-api-6).
read: FSD S1 A2.2 and A2.4 as the write path for an appraisal, with S5 as a reader.
confirm: Solution architect with S5, before wave 3 system test
impact: Two writers of the appraisal record would leave the floor price on a value the case never accepted.

text: The valuation order is raised through the rwb-integration contract, which owns the SVAF interface and its retries; this service records the order, its date, the rule version and the limit applied.
why: Arch v5 gives rwb-integration the interface configuration and the outbound items, and gives this service no outbound path of its own.
read: FSD S1 A2.1's SVAF order as a business step whose delivery belongs to the integration service.
confirm: Solution architect with the integration lead, before wave 3 system test
impact: A direct SVAF call from this service would create a second integration owner and a second retry policy.

text: The route timers are durable timers inside RouteDecisionWorkflow set through the workflow kit, and a breach is reported on the timer path that rwb-case owns; no Quartz table, connection or job is used.
why: Arch v5 replaces the shared Quartz tables with a Temporal Schedule or a durable timer in the owning service (DP-10).
read: FSD S1 A2.12's timer requirement, with the mechanism read as the workflow kit.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S1-012; Section 6 FR-S1-026; Section 9; Section 10
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 system test
impact: A Quartz dependency would put this service back on a retired shared table.

text: EV-28 stays AgentRunCompleted, produced by rwb-agent; the route agent's answer reaches this service through the agent contract, and this service's own decision output travels in RouteDecided.
why: Arch v5 slide 43 and the Ownership Map both make EV-28 P10's event.
read: The Temporal design slide's EV-28 citation as the agent event, not as a new event of this service.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S1-017, FR-S1-018; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S1-04
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 system test
impact: If a second event is created for the agent answer, the topic and its consumers must be added to the catalogue.

text: The appraisal-age check runs as a step of RouteDecisionWorkflow when the decision starts, when it is reopened and when an appraisal arrives; this service adds no Temporal Schedule until the job map gives it one.
why: The job map lists no S1 job and retires the five-minute timer check.
read: FSD S1's 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer' as a trigger class, satisfied by the workflow start and the arrival of an appraisal.
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 release
impact: A missed appraisal order is silent until a stale value reaches the decision.

text: The route rules are evaluated from the embedded Drools kit with the universal package in force and a route package added when Phase 2 lands; the package and rule version are recorded on every decision, and the rule owner is named in rwb-decision.
why: The Temporal design records no S1 package yet and keeps governance central in rwb-decision.
read: FSD S1's rule rows (BR-S1-001 to BR-S1-012) as the requirement that every value and rule is versioned data.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S1-005, CAP-S1-006; Section 6 FR-S1-012, FR-S1-015; Section 12 OQ-S1-11
confirm: Center of excellence analyst with P7, before wave 3 release
impact: A decision taken on an unnamed rule version cannot be reproduced in an audit.

text: The eight routes are named as Architecture v5 slide 3 names them and their numbers are held as versioned reference data; this document prints no number where the sources disagree.
why: The Temporal design records the route-numbering conflict as an open point.
read: FSD S1 A2.12's route start as a reference-data lookup rather than a hard-coded number.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S1-012; Section 6 FR-S1-025; Section 12 OQ-S1-08
confirm: Business analyst, S1 with P7, before wave 3 system test
impact: A wrong number starts the wrong route, which is the most expensive failure this service can make.

text: E3 consumes the published valuation and payoff contract and its fake, and the capabilities themselves release with S1 in wave 3.
why: The BRD records the dependency and the run cannot move a release date.
read: FSD S1 A2.1 and A2.6 as an E4 capability that E3 needs earlier, met by a contract rather than by a release.
confirm: Solution architect, before E3 system test
impact: Without the contract and its fake, E3 deed-in-lieu cannot be tested and E3 slips.

text: The four messages this service shows come from the catalogues of the services that own them (P1, P4, P7 and the general set), and this service adds no message of its own.
why: Every message ID in the FSD belongs to another service.
read: FSD S1's validation rows as reuse of the platform message standard rather than as a new catalogue.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S1-011, FR-S1-020; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S1-14
confirm: Business analyst, S1, before wave 3 release
impact: A copied wording drifts from the owning service and fails the Thai and English review.

text: Every route approval limit is read from the versioned delegation table of rwb-access at run time, and the level applied and the approver are recorded on the decision.
why: DL18 is open and the table belongs to P4; the principle that every limit is a versioned row applies.
read: FSD S1 A2.8 and A2.9 as an approval requirement whose limits are data.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S1-008, CAP-S1-009; Section 6 FR-S1-019, FR-S1-021; Section 8.2; Section 12 OQ-S1-10
confirm: Risk with the product heads, before wave 3 release
impact: A hard-coded limit is an approval taken by the wrong role.

text: The valuation record, the route decision and the route agent output carry a classification from the working labels of this document and a retention class whose period stays open under DL26.
why: NFR-047 and DL26 hold the classification scheme and the periods open.
read: FSD S1's field catalog as the field set to classify, with the classification supplied from the program requirement.
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 3 release
impact: An unclassified record cannot be masked, archived or disposed of on a stated rule.

text: This document stays at status Draft with an empty approval table, and the missing requirements approval is carried as an assumption.
why: The governing BRD is Draft, its approval table is empty, and the run records no verification stop (U8).
read: The playbook's requirements approval gate as a later step, not as a precondition of this run.
confirm: Product Owner, after this run
impact: Nothing here is approved until the Product Owner and the FDA sign, so no downstream build may treat it as baselined.

text: The route decision record holds the routes considered, the values and returns used, the recommendation with its reasons, confidence and alternatives, the approval with its level and approver, and the rule and model versions; the physical field list is left open.
why: No source gives a field list for the route decision or the route agent output.
read: REQ-S1-005 and NFR-033 as the content the record must hold, with the field list to follow.
confirm: Data architect, before the S1 DB story
impact: Without the content the decision cannot be reproduced, which fails NFR-033 at the first audit.

text: The inherited history carries FSD S1 version 3 in full and marks versions 1 and 2 as not specified in the sources read.
why: The FSD gives no version table and its change note covers only v2 to v3.
read: FSD S1 document control as the only history available.
confirm: Business analyst, S1, at the next FSD version
impact: A reconstructed history would be indistinguishable from a sourced one.

text: This is the first PRD of the S1 family, so version 1 is the next version and no earlier version is superseded.
why: The folder 03 Requirements and specifications/PRD holds no S1 file before this run.
read: Rules R8.2 (the next version is the highest of the family plus 1) applied to an empty family.
confirm: Product Owner, at approval
impact: If a parallel draft exists, the numbering of this family has to be reconciled.

text: The release dates E3 31 January 2027, E4 28 February 2027 and E8 30 June 2027 are copied from the release plan, marked tentative, and no date is raised as a gap.
why: Rules U7 and R8.5: dates unchanged and tentative, and a date is never a gap.
read: Program BRD v4 section 8 as the only release plan.
confirm: Program manager, at each monthly release
impact: A date change is a change of the release plan, not of this document.

text: This service's delivery wave (3) equals the business epic wave of E4 (3), so no wave conflict is raised for S1.
why: Rules R5.6 raise one conflict gap per service and business epic only where the waves differ.
read: BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 7.3 (S1 3, business epic wave 3) against Arch v5 slide 41 (S1 wave 3).
confirm: Solution architect, at wave 3 planning
impact: If E4 moves earlier, the contract-first slice becomes the only E3 and E4 path.

text: Every owner named in this document is a role or a service code taken from the Ownership Map or the BRD; no person is named.
why: Rules U3 and R8.1: roles only, no names of people anywhere.
read: BRD and FSD role names as written, and the Ownership Map service codes.
confirm: Product Owner, at approval
impact: A named owner would have to be replaced by a role before publication.

text: REQ-S1-001 to REQ-S1-008 are both the FSD requirement IDs and the program requirement IDs, and the BRD states the same intent as BR-016 to BR-021, so coverage is read at both levels.
why: The program BRD section 5.8, the FSD requirements-served table and BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 8.2 carry the same eight requirements under two ID sets.
read: The program ID as the business need and the BRD row as its restatement, one column for each in the trace.
confirm: Business analyst, at approval
impact: A future renumbering of either set has to keep the mapping row in section 11.2.
